why: No standalone AI statute exists; Niger's only enacted AI-specific provisions (Art. 1, 52, 57 declaration obligation) sit inside this consolidated data-protection law, the nearest thing to an operative AI instrument.
Dissolution of the HAPDP, the authority Article 57 assigns AI-operator declarations to -- an institutional movement directly bearing on AI regulation's enforcement machinery.

A distinct earlier event: national validation of the digital-development policy that could host future AI measures, the clearest digital-policy movement of the window short of AI-specific legislation.
The founding and still-operative e-commerce/electronic-transactions statute itself, captured complete from the Journal Officiel.
Council adoption of the ANCE implementing decree under Article 17-18 of the 2019 law, the concrete institutional step operationalising trust-service and e-signature certification.
A distinct later regulatory act: a ministerial arrêté placing commercial Wi-Fi provision under a declaration regime with ARCEP.
The founding statute creating the national statistical system and INS, still cited as the governing framework in INS's own 2024 status report.
Earlier, distinct preparatory step: INS's own committee had drafted the reform ordinance and transmitted it to the Secretariat General of Government, reported at the SYNPIS congress.
The completed governmental step: Council of Ministers adoption of the ordinance and decrees re-founding the statistical system, CNS and INS.
The founding and, on the evidence available, still-operative access-to-information statute itself, captured complete.
Creation of the ONC, the transition-era media/information regulator whose powers the later media-suspension event exercises -- a distinct institutional founding act.
A distinct, completed exercise of regulatory power restricting public access to international media sources.
The operative national data-protection statute, establishing the HAPDP's mandate and the transfer/adequacy regime -- the instrument itself, not commentary.
The single most significant institutional movement in the window: reported abolition of the HAPDP and transfer of its functions to two ministries.
A distinct event: adoption of the biometric civil-registry reform and creation of the ANEI, explicitly framed as respecting data-protection principles and digital sovereignty.

Articles 31 and 62-63 of this consolidated law are Niger's operative domestic rule on transferring personal data abroad (prior HAPDP authorisation plus adequacy); no in-window Niger-specific movement was found, only non-binding regional (ECOWAS/AES) developments after Niger's 2025 ECOWAS withdrawal.

Article 35 of this statute is the legal basis for Niger's Référentiel général d'interopérabilité; no dedicated technical referentiel or implementing decree was found published, so the founding statute is the baseline.
Council adoption of the civil-registry ordinance and ANEI creation, explicitly framed as remedying the deficit of interoperability among Niger's registration systems.
A distinct, later implementing decree expressly defining interoperability mechanisms between the civil-registry and population registers.

Niger's own founding domestic act authorising ratification of the AU Malabo Convention; the AU's own treaty-status record for the same ratification is already held in the base (DUP-EXACT), so this Nigerien communiqué takes the baseline slot.
Creation of ANCE and CNAC, operationalising trust-service certification and cybersecurity institutions compatible with international digital-trust and cybersecurity norms.
A distinct, completed international accession: WIPO's own depositary notification of Niger's accession to the Marrakesh Treaty, entering into force 20 October 2026.
The nearest thing to a measured, dated independent assessment of open political/policy debate in Niger, with explicit sub-scores and score-change notes tied to the post-coup transition.
A concrete, dated prosecution of journalists for relaying information about a government fund, under the amended cybercrime law.
A distinct event targeting a different channel of policy debate: mass suspension of civil-society organisations by the Ministry of the Interior.

The current, operative annual budget law itself (ordonnance n°2025-44), the controlling domestic appropriation instrument, even though the ministry's page does not expose a digital-specific line item.
The most digital-specific movement: validation of a budgeted 27-project roadmap for the national e-Health blueprint, with its own budget and financing mechanisms.
A distinct, general domestic budget movement in the window: the Council of Ministers' rectification of the 2026 budget law.
The operative bilateral digital-infrastructure agreement itself -- a signed protocole d'entente on the Niger-Chad fibre-optic interconnection -- rather than a description of Niger's partnerships.

A distinct, completed event: signature of a package of bilateral accords and MoUs at the close of the Niger-Algeria Joint Cooperation Commission. Only one progress item survives the screen -- a second candidate (national mobile-network control platform inauguration) was already held in the base (DUP-EXACT) and a third (Niger-Russia MTUCI protocol) was dropped on inadmissible origin (Pravda network).
The World Bank's own dedicated 'private sector investment raised through the project' indicator, quantifying realised non-state finance mobilised for Niger's digital connectivity.

A distinct non-state-finance-mobilisation event: a UNCDF/EU/OACPS catalytic grant enabling a Nigerien fintech to deploy a digital-payment platform at public universities. Only one progress item survives the screen -- a second candidate (a USD 250M IDA credit) is multilateral/state finance, not non-state, and was left unselected on that ground.
